speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your symptoms in detail, specifically regarding the fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and the location of the enlarged lymph nodes you mentioned.

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those systemic symptoms—significant weight loss, night sweats, and abdominal pain—are concerning for a malignancy or chronic infection. Can you tell me if the enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes are hard, fixed to the surrounding tissue, or tender to the touch?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The painless, fixed nature of your supraclavicular lymphadenopathy is a very serious sign. To differentiate between lymphoma, metastatic cancer, or tuberculosis, I need to evaluate your abdomen and lungs.

DIAGNOSIS READY: I require a CT scan of the chest and abdomen to evaluate for lymphoma or metastatic malignancy.
